answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by tying identity to a slashable stake bond plus unique vouchers from already-staked peers. Each fake account is just a mirror of one operator, but every new identity must lock fresh value and gather a distinct thread of endorsements that cannot be copied. Keys minted from copper and air buy nothing; when fraud is found the bond is slashed. So each extra Sybil costs a real bond and risks forfeiture, making a large attack linearly expensive and self-defeating.
